body:
jumangi@my-deja.com wrote:

>   TK's activities, and the Manifesto that supposedly justified them,
> occured during right-wing White-House administrations with the
> singular exception of Jimmy Carter.  Therefore, perceptions which
> want to claim reference to today's circumstances cannot in general
> be contemporaneous with the political background of his Manifesto.

Oh, c'mon.  Politicians are puppets who are unconcerned with helping
society; they just want to get elected.  Democrats and Republicans are
basically the same.  In the past the Republicans were more socially to the
right, and the Democrats were more to the left economically (I believe).
The Republican presidents of the last couple of decades have all been
clowns -- this includes "senile Ronnie".

>    What is "reverse McCarthyism?"

For lack of a better term, I used it.  PC and McCarthyism, though having
similar effects, are very different.

>   Closer examination of TK's actual words reveals your misreading.
> His criticism addressed the -side-effects- of unintended consequences
> engendered by conservative support for "technological progress and
> economic growth ... causing rapid changes in all _other_ aspects of
> a society ... [which] inevitably break down traditional _values_."
> Those remarks aren't directly addressing conservative _economic_ideals_
> which incidentally coincided with that "technological progress and
> economic growth" TK criticized -elsewhere- in the Manifesto, but the
> "other aspects" such as disintegration of "traditional values," that
> are constituent impacts upon _social_ policies.

Yes, he criticized the economic focus of conservatives to the extent that,
in his view, it creates social instability and breaks down traditional
values.  His concern over preserving the values of society was actually very
conservative.  When was the last time you heard a liberal politician talk
about family values?  (Al Gore just did, only to seperate himself from his
amoral cohort.  That was the first time I had ever seen a liberal do such a
thing, though).

> Could you manage to
> elaborate on where such "misinterpretation" really occurs?  You have
> offered the definition/characterization of "PC" as a condition of
> being "automatically right."

Perceiving to be automatically right.

> Continuing to run with your definition,
> doesn't it necessarily follow that meddling by those who are granted
> "automatic rights" to do so, is also "automatically right?"  Or were
> you about to say that "PC" means something other than the state of
> being "automatically right?"  More clarification, please.

Your sophistry is noted.  You are totally changing my words, to suit your
own weak, distorted conclusions.
